content.thinking:
The deploy timestamp lines up exactly with the onset, and rule_reading dropping sharply while everything else stays flat points to this being output-quality degradation from a model version change (v1 to v2), not a failed-request issue — the rollout converged cleanly with no compatibility break. I'm now weighing whether this counts as a config-induced failure since the model version is set in values-production.yaml, or whether it's purely an output-quality classification.

Looking at the taxonomy description, output-quality-degradation takes precedence whenever a revision lands at the onset and only rule_reading moves while request-level metrics stay flat — exactly what's happening here with the categoriser's model swap. The fix isn't about the deployment config itself but about the model or its inputs disagreeing, so rolling back would only mitigate, not truly resolve it. I'll classify this as output-quality-degradation with subject categoriser.model, transitioning from v1 to v2, with no faulting service since it's internal to io-shop.

hypotheses.subject: categoriser.model
hypotheses.summary: The 08:42 deploy switched the categoriser model from v1 to v2. Every request-level series (error_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, request_volume, cpu/memory) stayed at its pre-incident baseline through the onset, while rule_reading - the categorisation confidence score the paging rule watches - stepped from ~0.90 down to ~0.40 at exactly that minute and stayed there. The rollout has converged (3/3 replicas on the new revision), ruling out an in-flight split, and the only change in the diff is the categoriser.model value, not application code. This is a model answering with less confidence/sense than before rather than a service failing requests - quality degraded, not availability or latency.
